chapter: The circus dream and choosing the clarinet
title: Calliopes on Streckfus riverboats and Baton Rouge's river
summary: Riverboats coming to Baton Rouge announced themselves with calliopes; Joe describes the town on its hill above the Mississippi.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Working the Streckfus riverboats with Fate Marable

blocks.x: They didn't only use a live calliope on the circuses; they used them on some of the riverboats. Like when the steamer Capitol or the Streckfus Line boats that Louis and them played on, or the St. Paul or the Steamer Sidney, when they came to Baton Rouge, they'd have excursions going out of Baton Rouge, and the only way you'd know is that they would be in town, and they came town five miles out -- they'd start playing the calliope. Then
everybody would light out for the waterfront, just to see this boat come inn and hear that calliope.
Which way was Baton Rouge situated on the river?

Baton Rouge sits way on top of a hill. And as you'd come to the capital.. Huey Long built the Capital building. Baton Rouge was sort of a part of that. They had a big levee, you know. And you had to walk down to get to the river on account of the high water.
So that the Mississippi from New Orleans flowed west and a little north into Baton Rouge, and then cut out...
Yes, and then went to New Orleans, which was ninety mills, and emptied into the Gulf of Mexico. Naturally, it starts up in Minnesota.
